Senses.Explanation: In the institutional compound 'the two ranks' or 'the two divisions' (兩序), rank or division (序) names one of the two sides of a Chan community's offices. The Baizhang Regulations labels its sixth chapter 'the chapter on the two divisions' (兩序章), then identifies 'head monks of the western division' (西序頭首) and 'officers of the eastern division' (東序知事). Recorded sayings use 'the two divisions' for the office-holders who request an ascent to the hall, receive thanks, or support the community. Baiyu's record says that the two divisions served mutually as arms and elbows and acted reciprocally as host and guest (兩序交為肘臂、互作主賓).
Senses.Note: This is the Chan-institutional use found especially in the fixed compound 'the two divisions' (兩序). The corpus itself supplies the western-division/eastern-division subdivision; the entry does not infer duties beyond the stated labels and recorded deployments.

Occurrences.Kwic: 兩序章第六西序頭首東序知事
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Baizhang Regulations (勅修百丈清規) table of contents names chapter six as 'the chapter on the two divisions' (兩序章) and immediately lists the 'head monks of the western division' (西序頭首) and 'officers of the eastern division' (東序知事).

Occurrences.Kwic: 於中多賴兩序交為肘臂、互作主賓
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baiyu's Recorded Sayings (百愚禪師語錄) says, 'within this, much depended on the two divisions serving mutually as arms and elbows and acting reciprocally as host and guest' (於中多賴兩序交為肘臂、互作主賓).

Senses.Explanation: In a title or section heading, a preface (序) is introductory prose placed before a recorded-sayings collection, anthology, or edition. The graph commonly follows the work title, as in 'Preface to the Recorded Sayings of the Monk Foyan' (佛眼和尚語錄序), 'Preface to the Extensive Record of the Monk Yongjue' (永覺和尚廣錄序), and 'Preface to the Recorded Sayings of the Monk Sanfeng Cang' (三峰藏和尚語錄序).
Senses.Note: The title or heading determines this bibliographic sense. Translate the heading rather than treating the graph as part of a master's name or the work's main title.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄). The heading is the 'Preface to the Recorded Sayings of the Monk Foyan of Longmen in Shuzhou' (舒州龍門佛眼和尚語錄序).

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄). The repeated editorial heading identifies the 'Preface to the Extensive Record of the Monk Yongjue' (永覺和尚廣錄序).

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of the Monk Sanfeng Cang (三峰藏和尚語錄). The heading names the preface and its author, Xiong Kaiyuan (熊開元).

Senses.Explanation: In running prose, sequence or order (序) names an ordered progression. The Jingde-era lamp record says that beginning students did not know the sequence (初心後學未知次序). Konggu Daocheng's record says that matters for someone newly entering have an order (初進工夫，一一皆有次序) and names taking refuge and requesting instruction first (皈依請益為先). These witnesses state order directly; they do not turn the graph into a technical Chan category.
Senses.Note: This sense is represented through the transparent compound 'sequence/order' (次序). It is kept separate from the bibliographic preface and the institutional rank/division senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 其有初心後學未知次序。山僧所以不惜口業。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde-era Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄) says, 'there are beginning students who do not know the sequence; therefore this mountain monk does not begrudge the fault of speech' (其有初心後學未知次序。山僧所以不惜口業).

Occurrences.Kwic: 若問初進工夫，一一皆有次序，皈依請益為先
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Konggu Daocheng's Recorded Sayings (空谷道澄禪師語錄), in an instruction, says, 'if one asks about the work of first entering, each matter has its sequence; taking refuge and requesting instruction come first' (若問初進工夫，一一皆有次序，皈依請益為先).

Occurrences.Kwic: 觀其超然生死，實踐可知。因次序其行實，乃為之銘曰：
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A biographical notice says that the writer therefore put the subject's deeds in order before composing the inscription.
